rationale: The retained execution of the first experiment reproduced the witness: on the re-added voter (node 3, voter, leader 1 unchanged) the Propose invocation had not returned after 1200 ms, returned only with 'context deadline exceeded' when the caller's own 2500 ms deadline expired, and its payload never reached any node's committed entries; the never-removed member (node 2, same leader) returned in 0 ms and committed, and the same node 3 invocation returned in 0 ms and committed after a forced leader change. The first harness named the result events of all three operations 'propose_result', so each comparison also tried to evaluate the other operations' result events, failed their prerequisites and reported 'unknown' with missing indices. This update corrects the interpretation with the retained receipt, answers the open source gap, and submits a successor experiment whose per-operation event names make each comparison evaluate only its own operation.

experiment.revision_reason: Observation and comparison change: the witness, control and repair operations now emit distinctly named events (witness_invocation/witness_result/witness_release/witness_commit, control_invocation/control_result/control_commit, repair_leader_change/repair_invocation/repair_result/repair_commit, plus readd_applied and remove_applied) instead of sharing the names propose_invocation/propose_result/commit_observation/conf_change_applied. The scenario, prefix, node set, timings and measured fields are unchanged; the added witness_release comparison records that the blocked invocation ended only through the caller's context deadline. Rationale: with shared result-event names, each comparison also had to evaluate the other operations' result events, whose prerequisites are absent, so its outcome was reported as unknown with missing indices even though the decisive observations were complete.

scope.description: Three real raft nodes (ids 1,2,3) driven through the async Node API in one process: Ready handling with storage appends, conf-change application through Node.ApplyConfChange, and direct message delivery. Node 1 campaigns and becomes leader in the initial configuration {1,2,3} supplied by the storage ConfState; a remove-3 conf change and then an add-3 conf change are proposed on the leader and applied on every node. Then (a) Node.Propose is invoked on re-added node 3 while leader 1 is unchanged, (b) Node.Propose is invoked on never-removed node 2, and (c) after forcing a leader change (node 2 campaigns at term 2), Node.Propose is invoked again on node 3. Each invocation records whether it returned, the returned error, the elapsed time, the observed voter status and leader, and whether the payload reached any node's committed entries.
assumptions: Message delivery between the three in-process nodes is reliable and ordered per sender; no ticks are delivered, so the leader stays stable until the experiment forces the leader change.
Storage appends of Ready.Entries happen before the Ready's messages are dispatched, so durability precedes replication as the documented usage requires.

The removal and re-addition are the committed conf changes the driver applies; node 3 applies its own removal and re-addition through Node.ApplyConfChange, and no other code path sets the run loop's proposal gate.
excluded: RawNode.Propose (no proposal gate exists on that path)
Network faults: delivery is reliable, so non-delivery cannot be attributed to message loss

experiment.prefix: Start nodes 1,2,3 with a MemoryStorage per node whose ConfState voters are {1,2,3} (captured test helper withPeers). Node 1 campaigns at term 1 and becomes leader; every node then reports leader 1 and node 1 has applied the initial entry. Propose a remove-3 ConfChange on node 1 and wait until node 3's applied entries contain it and node 3's own configuration excludes node 3 (voter=false). Propose an add-3 ConfChange on node 1 and wait until node 3's applied entries contain it and node 3's configuration includes node 3 again (voter=true) with leader still 1. Then emit the observations for the three invocation cases and the forced leader change.
experiment.responsibility: Client-facing obligation of the Node interface: a Propose invocation on a voting member whose leader is known must either reach a proposal outcome (appended locally or forwarded to the leader) or return an error to the caller; a caller cannot retry a proposal whose invocation never returns.

comparisons.description: The invocation on the re-added voter did not return inside the observation window although that node's own configuration lists it as a voter and its leader is 1.
The blocked invocation ended only when the caller's own context deadline expired; raft never produced a proposal outcome for it.
The re-added voter's payload never appeared in any node's committed entries within the window.
Control: the never-removed member's invocation on the same leader returned immediately.
Control: the never-removed member's payload was committed on all three nodes, so the leader, replication and the proposal path were healthy.
After the forced leader change, the same invocation on node 3 returned immediately.
After the forced leader change, node 3's payload was committed, so the earlier block was not a property of node 3's state machine.

interpretations.rationale: Retained execution 43a04622beef40588679c6cf1c40d6ad (completed, exit 0) reproduced the predicted difference. Admission and prerequisites: the re-admission of node 3 was applied on node 3 at index 4 (change add, ok true, voter true, leader 1, term 1) with the context event at index 5 (node 3, voter true, leader 1) and the invocation admitted at index 6 (node 3, phase after_readmission, leader 1, deadline 2500 ms). Result: the invocation had still not returned after 1200 ms (index 7, returned false, elapsed_ms 1200, err empty, voter true, leader 1) and it released only with 'context deadline exceeded' at 2500 ms (index 8); its payload was in no node's committed entries (index 9, present false, observed_nodes null). The same call on never-removed node 2, same leader 1, returned in 0 ms (index 11) and its payload was committed on all three nodes (index 12); the same node 3 call returned in 0 ms (index 15) and committed on all three nodes (index 16) once node 3 observed leader 2 after the forced campaign (leader change 1->2 at term 2). The source account explains exactly this difference: the run loop's proposal gate is assigned only at node.go:374 (observed leader exists), node.go:377 (no leader) and node.go:426 (local member removed), and the re-admission conf change cannot match the removal guard because okBefore is false once the node's own Progress entry was deleted (node.go:401-412), so MsgProp is enqueued onto a nil channel in stepWithWaitOption (node.go:525) and can end only via the caller's context or node stop. The witness therefore records a proposal duty that is neither forwarded nor rejected while the member is a voter with a known leader, and the control excludes the rival explanations 'the leader or cluster was stalled' and 'the node is not a member / does not know a leader'.
counterevidence: node.go:407-411 acknowledges the mechanism as improvised ('propc is reset when the leader changes ... This isn't very sound and likely has bugs'). This explains how the wart arose and the leader-change dependence, but it is neither a calling restriction nor a protection: the re-added voter is permitted to call Propose, and the snapshot contains no other re-arm path (node.go:374/377/426 are the only assignments).

The blocked invocation is bounded by the caller's context (index 8: context deadline exceeded), so this is a bounded interval under a stable leader, not an unbounded deadlock; a caller with an unbounded context is not released.
Index 16 (repair) shows a successful invocation on the same node after leadership changed, so the defect is specific to the gate's re-arm condition and not a general failure of node 3.
limitations: The retained run's framework comparison outcomes were 'unknown' with missing indices for every comparison because the first harness gave the three operations' result events the same names, so each comparison also evaluated the other operations' result events. The decisive events above are complete and were re-checked locally with the framework comparator against the successor harness, where all seven comparisons evaluate as complete holds; the successor experiment is submitted for a fresh retained execution.

Scope is the async Node API path (node.run loop) in the captured snapshot; RawNode.Propose has no such gate and is not claimed to be affected. No tick was delivered and delivery was reliable, so the observation does not characterize network faults.
The block is reproduced for a node removed and re-added by committed conf changes with the same leader; variants with other conf change forms (joint/autoleave, learner demotion) were not executed.

3592ccaf01864f56aaf06d54a3f97423-gap-0.explanation: There is no such path in the captured snapshot. The run loop's proposal gate variable is assigned only three times (node.go:374 arms it when a leader is observed, node.go:377 clears it when no leader is observed, node.go:426 clears it after applying a conf change that removed the local member), and node.go:525 is the only read used for proposals. Re-addition is not handled: the removal guard at node.go:412-427 requires okBefore (the local node was in the configuration before this conf change), which is false when a node that is absent from its own configuration applies its own re-add. Responsibility therefore lies with the node wrapper, which offers no re-arm for re-admission; the application can only recover by obtaining a leader change or by using RawNode directly.

knowledge.assertion: propc is armed only on observed leader change and is left nil after a re-admission
MsgProp on a nil propc blocks until context expiry or node stop
the raft state machine returns ErrProposalDropped for a removed leader instead of blocking
